 JUDGMENT

All these appeals arise out of common judgment and award dated 29.01.2015 passed by Reference Court in 4/2011, 8/2011, 12/2011 and 13/2011 and separate judgment and award in LAC 2/2014 passed by the Court of Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47692006/
9 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB the Learned Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Arsikere (hereinafter referred for short as "Reference Court").

The claimants' have challenged impugned judgment for enhancement of compensation and second respondent challenged the same on the ground that market value determined is unreasonable.
All these - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB appeals are taken up together and common judgment is passed.

4. All these appeals arises out of common acquisition proceedings initiated by Respondent No.1 to 3 for acquisition of lands for the purpose of conversion of Railway track from meter-gauge to broad-gauge, from Arsikere to Kadur.
As already stated above, except LAC No.2 of 2011, other cases were clubbed together and common evidence was recorded.
In LAC No.2/2011, separate evidence was recorded.
However, market value of land acquired in all the above said cases were determined by the Reference Court as Rs.300/- per square feet.
5. It appears, the claimants in other connected land acquisition cases, so also, the respondents in the said cases have not challenged the judgment and award passed by the Reference court.
We refer to the parties as their rank before the Reference court for sake of convenience.

sentences.text: It is the case of claimants that the Respondent-State had acquired lands belonging to claimants herein along with some other lands, situated at AncheKoppalu, Kalanakoppalu Village and Arasikere Village of Arsikere Taluk in Hassan District for the purpose of expansion of Arsikere-Birur Railway i.e. conversion of Meter gauge into Broad gauge.

As per the request of Respondent No.2,
Respondent No.1 and 3 initiated acquisition proceedings and acquired various properties including Survey Nos.337, 375, 377 and 378 etc., of Arsikere Village as well as lands situated in Kalanakoppalu village of Hassan District.
Portion of land belonging to claimants which are subject matter of LAC cases No.2/11, 4/11, 12/11, 8/11 and 13/11 were also acquired in the said Notification.
. The Government, i.e., SLAO, has initiated acquisition proceedings and published preliminary notification dated 29.06.2009.

The Reference Court, in the impugned judgment, at page No.5,
paragraph No.3 has mentioned in detail about the extent of land, survey number, its village, date of notification, date of acquisition, date of taking possession and date of notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, date of award and date of reference applications are mentioned and there is no need to reproduce the same.
It appears the SLAO had taken possession of all the acquired properties under the said Notification dated 29.06.2009 on the very same day, i.e., 29.06.2009.

Thereafter, the SLAO had issued final notification under Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.

The SLAO had considered different sale deeds of the properties sold nearby the acquired lands and passed general award dated 28.02.2010, fixing the market value of the said acquired land at Rs.66 per square feet.
Accordingly, notices were issued under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act to the claimants.

9. The claimants being aggrieved by the award/assessment of market value of the land acquired,
filed protest petition/application under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter for sake of brevity referred to as 'Land Acquisition Act').
In the month of July 2010, the said references were submitted to the Senior Civil Judge Court by the SLAO for determination of reference applications.

It appears out of the said reference cases, LAC Nos.1/11, 3/11, 4/11, 5/11,
6/11, 7/11, 8/11, 9/11, 10/11, 11/11, 12/11, 13/11 and 15/11 were clubbed together and common evidences were recorded.
10.
The claimants had examined PW1 to 16 and got marked Ex.P1 to P62.
Similarly, respondents examined RW1 and got marked exhibit R1.

In LAC No.2/2011, which was tried separately, claimant examined - 16 - Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47692006/
11 NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB PW1 and 2 and got marked exhibit P1 to 5.

Respondents examined RW1 and got marked Ex.R1.
11.

The Reference Court after hearing both the parties and appreciating evidence placed on record by both the parties, by impugned judgment and award dated 28.11.2014 and 29.01.2015, assessed the market value of the acquired land at Rs.300/- per square feet and also awarded other statutory benefits.

12. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award passed by the reference court in LAC No.2/2011, 4/2011, 8/2011, 12/2011 and 13/2011, claimant as well as respondent No.2 have filed aforesaid appeals.

Claimants in MFA 6518/ 2018 and 6514/2018 have filed appeal for enhancement of compensation and respondent No.2, has challenged the impugned award on the ground that the amount of compensation determined by the Reference court is on much higher side and unreasonable.
We have heard the arguments of the learned advocate for claimants as well as the Respondents- beneficiary of the acquisition proceedings and learned High Court Government Pleader for State.
14. The learned advocate for appellant-claimant has vehemently contended that the market value assessed by reference court is on much lower side.

As per Ex.P-29, the property value was Rs.408/-
per square feet.

However, the Reference court calculated the compensation on the basis of sale statistics, that is, considered two sale deeds i.e. Ex.P-27 and Ex.28 and on the basis of average sale price of the land, determined the amount of market value as Rs.300/-, which is on lower side.
The Reference Court ought to have considered Ex.P-29 alone for assessment of the market value.

The land acquired by the respondents in the above said appeals are situated nearer to the main road,
within city limits and it is admittedly situated nearby the railway track and it has all the - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB potentiality.
Moreover, the claimants were residing in the said land and had constructed house and well developed it.
However, it was acquired by the respondents without paying proper compensation.
Therefore, the determination of market value of the acquired land is on much lower side.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the market value from Rs.300/- to Rs.500/- per square feet.

15. The main contention of learned advocate for respondents beneficiary i.e. Railway Department is that the Reference Court has considered value of the property stated in Ex.P-27 and P-29 and taken average sale price of the lands sold under said sale deeds and assessed the market value as Rs.300/-
per square feet.
The Reference Court has rejected Ex.P-28 on the ground that the sale price of said land per square feet is Rs.36.73/- which is less than the market value determined by SLAO.

The said Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47692006/
12 finding of the Reference Court is erroneous.

sentences.text: . The learned advocate for railways has relied on judgment in the case of the GANGA KISAN SARKARI CHINI MILLS VS. GHASITA (D) AND ANOTHER1, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad has held that even if the market value of the land sold under sale deed is lesser than the market value determined by the SLAO, then also the said market value of the property covered under such sale deeds to be considered.

entities.text: GANGA KISAN SARKARI CHINI MILLS VS. GHASITA (D) AND ANOTHER1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Market values of the lands covered under all the sale deeds produced shall be considered.
Market values of the lands covered under all the sale deeds produced shall be considered.
Thereafter average sale price of lands of all sale deeds to be considered to assess market price of acquired lands.
If the said average market value is less than market value determined by SLAO then it shall not be considered to assess the market price.
Thereafter average sale price of lands of all sale deeds to be considered to assess market AIR 2004 Page number 15 - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB price of acquired lands.
If the said average market value is less than market value determined by SLAO, then it shall not be considered to assess the market value.

The Reference Court cannot reject a sale deed merely on the ground that market value of the lands sold under the sale deed is less than the market value of the lands assessed by the land Acquisition Officer.

Such sale deeds are also relevant and should be taken into account in order to arrive at the correct market value with the rider that Reference Court in no case award lesser compensation than awarded by the land acquisition officer.

In this case, if the Reference Court had taken into consideration Ex.P- 28 then the market value would be about Rs.200/- per square feet and odd and not Rs.300/- as wrongly assessed by the Reference Court.
In view of the said reasons, interference in the impugned judgment and award is required.

The learned HCGP supported submission of arguments of learned advocate to respondent No.2.
17.
Both the parties have relied on the few judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court as well as different High Courts.
18. From the above said contentions, following question arises for our determination.
"Whether the reference court is erred in determination of the market value and it needs to be interfered by this Court?"

sentences.text: Most of the facts of this case are not in dispute.
The nature of the property, extent of the property, ownership of the property, identity of properties etc are not in dispute.
Similarly, the date of Notification issued under Section 4(1) and 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act as well as notice issued under Section 12(2) of the Act are also not disputed.
Therefore, there is no need to - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB discuss about the same.

The respondents have contended before the Reference Court that application filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act is barred by time and the said contention was rejected by the Reference Court by assigning the valid reasons and it is not challenged in the present appeals.
Therefore, reconsideration of the same is not required.
As rightly observed by the Reference Court, the applications filed by the claimant-applicant are in time as per Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and hence it needs to be confirmed.
20. It is not in dispute that the property acquired were agricultural lands having potentiality and being used for residential purpose.

In Ex.P7, i.e., the award passed by the SLAO, he has stated that some of the lands acquired in the case were already converted for non- agricultural use and the claimants were also residing in the said property by constructing the houses.
Their names were entered in the property extract maintained by the - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB concerned Municipality.
Looking to the quality of the soil, they are fertile lands.

Considering all these factors as well as potentiality, the SLAO has considered the sale deeds pertaining to sites sold during the period of 2006 to 2009, determined the market value of the land as Rs.66/- per square feet.

21. The claimants have contended that assessment of/determination of market value by the Reference Court at the rate of Rs.300/- per square feet, is on lower side; however they did not place any materials on record during pendency of this appeal, to show that market values of near by land sold prior to notification were much more than as assessed by the reference court.
Under such circumstances, the said contentions do not hold any water.
More over even they did not explain as to how reference court had committed an err in the impugned judgment.
On the contrary the reference court - 24 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB considered market value on the basis of sale statistics i.e., sale deeds produced by the claimant/appellants.
Hence claimant cannot raise grievance about it.
22. The main contention of both the respondents is whether rejection of Ex.P-28 by the Reference Court is justifiable?
If Ex.P.28 is taken into consideration, then average market value would be around Rs.225/- per square feet.
However, the Reference Court has determined market value at the rate of Rs.300/-.

The Reference Court in the impugned judgment at Paragraph No.21 has observed Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47692006/
14

entities.text: Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that "If we calculate the market value as per Ex.P-28 sale deed, then under the said sale deed, 2.1/2 gunta of land was sold for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only).

If we calculate the value per square feet which comes to Rs.36.73/-, the said sale deed cannot be considered for the reason that the land was sold for Rs.36.73/- per square feet, which is below the award passed by the respondent in respect of the acquired lands.
In view of Section 25 of Land Acquisition Act, no compensation can be awarded, which is below the award passed by the SLAO.
Hence, Ex.P-28 is not taken into consideration to determine the market value".
23. The said observation is seriously challenged by the Respondent's/Beneficiary Railway Department.

According to their contention, as already stated above, in the case of Ganga Kisan Sarkari Chini Mills Vs. Ghasita (D) and another, (referred supra) the High Court of Allahabad has held that even though the market value of the land sold under a sale deed is lesser than the market value of a property determined by the SLAO, then also such sale statistics has to be considered and market value has to be determined.

entities.text: Ganga Kisan Sarkari Chini Mills Vs. Ghasita (D) and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, such determined market value should not be lesser than the amount of market value determined by the SLAO.

In view of the law laid down in this said judgment, it is a strenuous argument of the learned counsel appearing for the railways that the - 26 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB Reference Court ought to have considered Ex.P-28 for determination of market value of the acquired land.

24. It is pertinent to note that in Ex.P-28, the land sold was a site formed in Survey No.6/1 of Arsikere village, the said sale deed dated 02.02.2009 i.e., prior to initiation of acquisition proceedings.

Admittedly, there is no clear evidence regarding location of Survey No.6/1 i.e. there is no reference as to whether the said land is situated nearby the acquired land or it has same potentiality and other qualities as that of the land acquired in the present case.

On the contrary, in Ex.P-27, a site formed in Survey No.389/2 i.e. site No.64 measuring 30 x 40 sq. ft. i.e., 1,200 sq. ft.
was sold on 28.08.2008 for Rs.2,80,000/- and under Ex.P-29, site No.65 formed in Survey No.389/2 measuring 30 x 40 sq. ft. i.e., 1,200 sq.ft was sold for Rs.4,90,000/- and the property acquired in the present case are bearing Survey Nos.337, 375 and 377.

Looking to survey numbers, it appears the said - 27 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB Survey No.389/2 wherein site Nos.64 and 65 were formed and sold under Exs.P-27 and 29, are situated nearby the acquired property.

Under these circumstances, the property covered under Ex.P-28 is not at all relevant for determination of the market value of the property acquired under the present Notification, which are challenged in the present appeal.

Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47692006/
15

entities.text: Sri Prakash vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned advocate for both side could not explain situation of said land covered under Ex.P.28 and acquired properties.
It appears the claimants were not properly advised to place relevant materials on record, which do help the Reference Court to assess the proper market value of the property.
Therefore, rejection of Ex.P-28 is proper;

However, reason assigned by the Reference Court might not be justifiable in view of the findings of the Allahabad High Court in the case of Ganga Kisan Sarkari Chini Mills Vs. Ghasita (D) and another, (referred supra).

entities.text: Ganga Kisan Sarkari Chini Mills Vs. Ghasita (D) and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If we consider Ex.P-27 and 29 and - 28 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB determine the market value, taking average market value, then the findings of the Reference Court does not call for any interference in this appeal pertaining to assessment of the market value of the acquired land.
25. As discussed in the above paragraphs, there are no materials on record to hold that the determination of the market value by the Reference Court is incorrect.

Though the claimants in two cases, that is in LAC No.4/11 and 12/11 challenged the impugned judgment and award on the ground that the market value determined by the Reference Court is on lower side, but they did not place any other materials before this Court to hold that the determination of the market value by the Reference Court was incorrect or on lower side.

Similarly, the contentions of the Railways that rejection of Ex.P-28 and taking only two sale deeds i.e., Ex.P 27 and 29, was incorrect and because of that the Reference Court had wrongly determined the market value on higher side, i.e., Rs.300/-
- 29 - NC: 2023:KHC:41721-DB per square feet, is also not tenable because Ex.P-28 is pertaining to a different property bearing Survey No.6/1 and there is no material on record to show that the said land is adjacent to the land acquired in the present case.

It may be true that the reasons assigned by the Reference Court for rejection of Ex.P-28 is incorrect, but looking to the situation of the property covered in Ex.P-27 and 29, they appear to be situated near and having same status as that of the land acquired in this case, than the property bearing Survey No.6/1.
Therefore, Ex.P-28 is not a relevant document to be considered in the present case for determination of the market value.
Other judgments relied by both side is pertaining to manner of assessment of market value of land acquired.
They are not relevant to the facts of circumstances of present case, since point of dispute in this case is very narrow i.e., about Ex.P.28.
Hence not discussed in this judgment.
We do not find any reasons to interfere in the findings of the Reference Court in the impugned judgment and award passed in LAC No.2/2011, 4/2011, 8/2011, 12/2011 and 13/2011.

Hence we answer above referred question in the negative and pass following:

Such sale deeds are also relevant and should be taken into account in order to arrive at the correct market value with the rider that Reference Court in no case award lesser compensation than awarded by the land acquisition officer.
